solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Siamese location on main line

definitions.note: the clue gives the breed, the answer names one colouring of it

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
L is the standard abbreviation for line
a point is a place or location

explanation.surface: Someone pinpoints where a Siamese person or thing sits along a main railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main line' looks like railways, but the main is an old word for the ocean. In an across clue, A 'on' B puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal-point is a Siamese cat whose face, ears, paws and tail are dark brown, the classic pattern of that breed.

clue.text: Actor finally in cast gets smallest part

indicators.note: the actor's closing letter sits inside the word meaning 'cast'

parts.note: to cast off skin or leaves is to shed them

indicators.note: 'finally' points to the closing letter of the word 'actor'

parts.note: last letter of 'actor'

explanation.surface: A cast list where the last actor gets the tiniest role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' reads as the actors in a play, but here it is the verb: to shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a tiny scrap or fragment, as in 'not a shred of evidence', so it is the least possible bit.

clue.text: One to depart this world like man strapped in tight?

parts.note: 'as' means like, in the same way as

indicators.note: someone strapped into a seat is held inside it, so the man goes inside the word for 'tight'

parts.note: taut means pulled tight
Ron is a man's name, a common crossword stand-in for 'man'

explanation.surface: A man strapped in tight, as if about to die and leave this world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depart this world' sounds like dying; the question mark hints it means literally leaving Earth. The strapped-in man then fits the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller literally leaves the planet, so the euphemism for death is taken at face value.

clue.text: Pawn courts one escaping wealthy tribal leader

indicators.note: the letter for 'one' escapes, leaving the word for 'wealthy' without it

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
atria are open inner courts of Roman houses
rich = wealthy; the I (one) then escapes, leaving RCH

explanation.surface: Someone pawns goods and goes to court to escape a rich chieftain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' and 'courts' both look like verbs; they are a chess piece and a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male head of a family or tribe, the elder who governs a clan.

clue.text: Wearing but a smile as fitness keeps love secure in Bury

indicators.note: the word for fitness keeps love and secure within it

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: the whole of that goes inside the word meaning bury

parts.note: health = fitness
love is nil, the zero shaped like O
to secure a prize is to get it

explanation.surface: A naked, grinning fitness fanatic in the Lancashire town of Bury, keeping love safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a real town near Manchester, and its capital letter disguises the verb. There are two nested containers: love and secure sit inside fitness, then that sits inside bury.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In the altogether' is a British idiom for stark naked, so someone dressed only in a smile qualifies.

clue.text: Meagre dinner though not badly cooked

indicators.note: food that is badly cooked is ruined, so these letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

explanation.surface: A skimpy dinner, though at least it was not badly cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' looks like it negates 'badly cooked', but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thin on the ground is scarce or sparse, which is what meagre describes: scanty supply.

clue.text: Day needed to bottle Irish rum

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the day word holds Irish

parts.note: Wed is the short form of Wednesday
IR is a standard abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A day set aside for bottling Irish rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink; in British English it is also an adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is British informal for strange or peculiar, as in 'a rum business', a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Sorted how to contain area round burning bush

indicators.note: the sorted letters wrap around the abbreviation for area
letters that are sorted are put into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as printed
a round thing is shaped like the letter O; joins the fodder
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone works out how to fence off the area around a burning bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The burning bush suggests Moses, but it is a plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Wahoo is a North American shrub, Euonymus atropurpureus, whose autumn leaves turn fiery red and so is also called burning bush.

clue.text: Metrical patterns in book one French friend carries

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the French friend carries the book, holding it inside

parts.note: ami is French for friend
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A French friend carries a book of verse full of metre.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the patterns are found in a book; 'in' just links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi is the Latin plural of iambus, a poetic foot of one unstressed then one stressed syllable.

clue.text: Made inedible with teeth, all at first tucking in

indicators.note: the letter is tucked inside the word for 'with teeth'

parts.note: dentured = fitted with dentures, false teeth

indicators.note: 'at first' takes only the opening letter of 'all'

parts.note: first letter of 'all'

explanation.surface: Food ruined by false teeth, with everyone tucking in at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking in' suggests eating, which fits the food surface, but it means insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Denatured alcohol has additives that make it unfit to drink, so denaturing makes a substance unfit for consumption.

clue.text: Repeatedly thanks plumber, finally turning taps

indicators.note: turning the whole string round makes it run back to front

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks, said here three times

indicators.note: 'finally' takes the closing letter of 'plumber'

parts.note: last letter of 'plumber'

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a plumber over and over for finally fixing the taps.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps look like the sink fittings a plumber turns; they are knocks, and the answer is a noun. TA is British informal for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat-a-tat is an imitative word for a series of sharp knocks, like repeated rapping on a door.

clue.text: Brutal Scotsman masking new and unpleasant whiff

indicators.note: a mask covers something, so the Scotsman's name covers the other letters

parts.note: Ian is the Scottish form of John, the crossword Scotsman
N is the abbreviation for new
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A cruel Scotsman trying to hide a fresh, nasty smell.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a hum is a stink as well as a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhuman describes cruelty lacking all compassion, the same savage quality as brutal.

clue.text: Cloth Asians wrap around copper piping inside

indicators.note: the word for piping goes inside the police abbreviation

parts.note: a copper is a policeman, and DI is Detective Inspector
piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: Cloth that people wrap around copper pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' seems to be the metal the cloth wraps; it is a police officer. 'Wrap around' belongs to the definition, not a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a long loincloth worn by men in India, wound round the waist and legs.

clue.text: Green specialist in City loves squeezing large marrow

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: the two loves squeeze the abbreviation for large between them

parts.note: love is zero, O, so two loves are OO
L is the abbreviation for large
the marrow of something is its core, its gist

explanation.surface: A vegetable expert in the City who loves pressing a large marrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Green and marrow suggest vegetables; green means environmental, and marrow is the essence of a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecologist studies living things and their environment, the scientific side of green politics.

clue.text: Faculty has objective bringing in Liberal

indicators.note: the word for objective brings the Liberal abbreviation inside it

parts.note: fair = objective, impartial
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A university faculty whose goal is to recruit a Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' reads as a university department and 'objective' as a goal; they are a talent and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty can mean a natural aptitude, and flair is a special talent or knack.

clue.text: Exploit ambassadors, visibly embarrassed having got down

parts.note: an exploit is a daring deed, a feat
HE, His Excellency, is how ambassadors are addressed
blushing shows embarrassment as a red face

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of diplomats, who blush after being brought low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got down' looks like dismounted or depressed; down here is soft plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the fine soft covering of birds, so a creature covered with it has grown plumage.

clue.text: Clear to me, suffering, one gets there eventually?

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone, clear-minded but in pain, says they will arrive in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a playful description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A latecomer arrives after the expected time, so they do reach the destination, just belatedly.

clue.text: Broccoli in clear base that's reconstituted

indicators.note: reconstituting something builds it up again in a different form

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Broccoli in a clear stock made up from a powder.
explanation.walkthrough: The soup-making surface is apt: dried stock is reconstituted, and the vegetable could go in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Calabrese is the common green variety of broccoli with large heads, named after Calabria in Italy.

clue.text: Policy statement complicated by means of it?

indicators.note: a complicated arrangement is tangled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A policy document made harder to follow by its own methods.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the surface is a gentle dig at political writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is the published declaration of a party's aims and intended policies, especially before an election.

clue.text: Wasted the bacon sandwiches one cut

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling, so the bacon phrase holds the numeral
something wasted is wrecked, so all the letters are scrambled

parts.note: anagram fodder
I is the Roman numeral one, joining the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone throws away the bacon sandwiches that one person made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' reads as food, fitting the bacon; it is the verb, putting I inside before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An aitchbone is the rump bone of cattle, and the joint of beef containing it is a butcher's cut.

clue.text: Some drivel in edition with ruling

indicators.note: 'some' of the following words means only part of their letters

parts.note: the letters run from the end of 'drivel' through 'in' into the start of 'edition'

explanation.surface: A published edition full of nonsense, including a court's decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling' looks like a legal judgment; it is the printed lines on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled paper has straight printed guide lines across it, so paper with ruling on it is lined.

clue.text: Pet having to tolerate an arboreal creature

parts.note: honey is an endearment, like pet or darling
to bear something is to put up with it

explanation.surface: A pet owner who has to put up with a tree-dwelling animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet is the British endearment, as in 'thanks, pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey bear is a name for the kinkajou and the sun bear, both animals that live and climb in trees.

clue.text: Fool around, producing explosive component

parts.note: a nit, or nitwit, is a fool
re means about, concerning, and around can mean about

explanation.surface: Messing about produces a piece of a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool around' looks like one phrasal verb; split it into a noun and a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, saltpetre, one of the three ingredients of gunpowder.

clue.text: Heard tropical disease is for the solver to deal with?

definitions.text: for the solver to deal with?

indicators.note: something heard is taken by ear, so the disease is judged by its sound

parts.note: yaws is a tropical skin infection

explanation.surface: A tropical illness that was overheard now becomes the reader's problem.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent yaws and yours sound the same. The solver is the one reading, so the answer is second person.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever belongs to the person addressed is theirs, and the person addressed by a crossword clue is its reader.

clue.text: Minimal information about English female in suit

indicators.note: the minimal information goes about, around, the English female pair

parts.note: a bit is the smallest unit of computer information
E is the abbreviation for English
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Scant details about an English woman wearing a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing, fitting the woman; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to be appropriate for, just as something that suits a person is proper to them.

clue.text: Duke in hat to see señorita's wiggle

indicators.note: the duke abbreviation goes inside the word for hat

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
D is the abbreviation for Duke

explanation.surface: A duke in a hat goes to watch a young Spanish woman wiggle.
explanation.walkthrough: The wiggle seems to be a dance; it is the squiggle over the N in señorita.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy mark written over Spanish ñ, and it appears in the very word señorita.

clue.text: Improve gag about old uniform

indicators.note: the word for gag goes about, around, the old and uniform letters

parts.note: to gag is to retch
O is the abbreviation for old
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Make an old uniform better by adding a joke about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' reads as a joke; here it is the verb meaning to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: To retouch a photo or painting is to make small corrections that enhance it.

clue.text: University student is clear to return gadget

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the student, is and clear run back to front

parts.note: L is a learner, the L-plate on a student driver's car
taken as printed
net profit is what you clear after costs

explanation.surface: A university student is free to hand back a device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'University student' looks like one person, but only the student letter is reversed; U stays in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially one used in the kitchen, so a useful device.

clue.text: 500 on ship wear formal clothes

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
re = on, concerning
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Five hundred passengers aboard a liner put on evening wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' seems to place the 500 aboard; it gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress for dinner means putting on evening attire, so the verb covers formal wear.

clue.text: Strip staff member giving support in tent

parts.note: a ridge is a long narrow strip of raised ground
a staff is a pole, and a pole is a structural member

explanation.surface: A strip search on an employee who works in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip staff member' reads as undressing an employee; it is two nouns, a strip of land and a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridgepole is the horizontal beam running along the top of a tent, holding up the canvas.
